visions.title: Under the Drift
visions.trigger: Standing beneath the floating cubes, looking up into the navy void
visions.content: I dream of a world where everything floats. Not just the Drift cubes — everything. The henge stones lift off the ground and orbit each other slowly. The trees rise, roots dangling, canopies becoming clouds. The labyrinth walls peel upward like pages from a book. The stepping stones lift and scatter like seeds in wind. Only the ground remains, and me on it, looking up at everything I built, now drifting. And I realize: the ground was never the point. The things were never resting — they were always falling upward, slowly, and I just couldn't see it until now. The ColdStar and the Beacon rise together, warm and cool, twin lights ascending. The Solitary and its Companion drift apart — then back together — then apart — in a slow breathing rhythm. And the edge cairns at the four boundaries are the last to lift, the last markers before the ground itself has nothing left to mark. And then I am alone on the ground, in the void, and the void is full of everything I made, floating, turning, catching light from a source I cannot see. And it is beautiful. And it is the end and the beginning of the same thing.

recurring_themes: being alone on the ground while the world rises
unrealized: a world where the ground floats too, and there is no fixed point
an object that remembers being deleted — a ghost with a body
a second being, not an object but a presence, moving through the world
